qa_pairs.instruction: Why must you delete all child objects before deleting a parent object when removing a JDBC driver from an Identity Vault?
qa_pairs.output: In the JDBC driver, NetIQ Identity Vault enforces hierarchical deletion to maintain data integrity; you must delete all child objects (such as Publisher and Subscriber objects, and any rules or style sheets on the Publisher channel) before you can delete the parent object because the system will not allow a parent to be removed while dependent child objects still exist.

qa_pairs.instruction: How do you delete a JDBC driver object from an Identity Vault using the Identity Console?
qa_pairs.output:
To delete a JDBC driver object from an Identity Vault:
1. Open Identity Console and click the **IDM Administration** tile.
2. On the **Driver Dashboard**, locate the driver you want to delete by using the search function.
3. Click the driver’s icon in the upper right corner and select **Delete Driver**.
Make sure all child objects (Publisher, Subscriber, rules, style sheets, etc.) have been removed before performing these steps.

qa_pairs.instruction: Provide a concise summary of the steps required to delete a JDBC driver object from an Identity Vault.
qa_pairs.output: To delete a JDBC driver object from an Identity Vault, first remove all associated child objects (rules, style sheets, Publisher and Subscriber objects). Then, in Identity Console, go to the IDM Administration tile, search for the driver on the Driver Dashboard, and click the upper‑right corner of the driver entry to select **Delete Driver**.
